1	# Project Context
2	
3	Last updated: 2026-09-03 (run_id 2026-09-03) — Initial creation. No prior `context.md` existed in
4	`/hms/projects/m1_sdp/M1-SDP/m1-sdp-qa-pipeline` at time of writing; this document was built from
5	scratch by reading the codebase at `/hms/projects/m1_sdp/M1-SDP/m1-sdp` (HEAD detached at tag
6	`3.0.68`, latest commit `2b8c7f561`).
7	
8	## Overview
9	- **m1-sdp** (hSenid Mobile "M1 Service Delivery Platform") is a large, long-lived telecom SDP:
10	  it provisions and mediates value-added services (SMS, USSD, BAS/premium billing, WAP push, MMS)
11	  between mobile network operator gateways (SMSC/UCP, USSD GW, SS7/Sigtran, ECGS charging) and
12	  content/service providers, plus back-office apps for provisioning, charging config, and CDR
13	  reporting.
14	- Multi-module Maven reactor (`pom.xml`, `groupId hsenidmobile.sdp`, `artifactId m1-sdp`,
15	  currently version `3.0.68`) containing ~50 modules of very mixed vintage: modern Spring Boot 3
16	  apps sit alongside 2008-era Ant/Ivy webapps in the same repo.
17	- Confirmed from `README.md`: runtime is OpenJDK 21, MySQL 8.4.4, Maven 3+; legacy modules still
18	  build with Ant + `HSENID_BUILD_COMMON`/`CXF_HOME` env vars, and depend on external
19	  hSenid-internal connector projects (`ajuba-connector`, `ussd-connector`, `spml-connector`)
20	  built separately from their own repos.
21	
22	## Tech Stack
23	- **Languages/runtime:** Java 21 (`pom.xml` `maven.compiler.target=21`); a few legacy modules
24	  historically targeted Java 1.6 (`module.properties` in `core-logic`, `compile.target.version=1.6`,
25	  though the parent POM now forces 21 repo-wide).
26	- **Modern stack (provisioning-v2, report-viewer-v2, cdrquery):** Spring Boot 3.4.5, Spring
27	  6.2.6, Thymeleaf + Tailwind CSS, Spring Security OAuth2 Client (Keycloak SSO), Hibernate
28	  6.6.13, MySQL Connector/J 9.3.0, Log4j2 2.25.1, Jasper Reports/POI/iText (report-viewer-v2),
29	  Spring Data JPA (cdrquery).
30	- **Legacy stack (dashboard, provisioning, reportviewer, cdragent, etc.):** Ant + Ivy builds,
31	  JSP/Struts-style webapps, CAS-based SSO (`modules/cas`), c3p0 connection pooling, ehcache.
32	- **Messaging/integration middleware:** Mule ESB 3.x-style custom runtime
33	  (`modules/mule-integration`, packaged as `sdp-mule-integration`), RocksDB used as a local
34	  durable queue/burst buffer (`RocksDbBasedBurstServerEventHandler.java`, plus
35	  `RocksDbBurstHandler_FlowDiagram.md` at repo root documenting that flow).
36	- **DB:** MySQL, schema name `sdp_sla` (seen in `core-logic.properties`, `sbl-v2` README),
37	  accessed via JDBC/Hibernate/c3p0; `docker-compose.yaml` at root spins up `mysql:5.6.51` for
38	  local dev alongside newer modules that assume MySQL 8.4.4 — **version mismatch, not confirmed
39	  which is authoritative for current dev**.
40	- **Build tools present:** Maven (root `pom.xml`, `mvnw`), Ant (`build.xml` at root and in most
41	  legacy modules), Ivy (`ivy.xml` in legacy modules), npm/Tailwind (`package.json` in
42	  provisioning-v2 and report-viewer-v2 for CSS build only).
43	- **Auth:** Keycloak OAuth2/OIDC for the three new Spring Boot apps (see Architecture), CAS for
44	  legacy dashboard/provisioning/reportviewer apps.
45	
46	## Architecture
47	- Overall style: **service-oriented monolith-of-modules** — one Maven reactor, many
48	  independently deployable components communicating over HTTP(S), SMPP, and Mule-mediated
49	  queues, sharing one MySQL database (`sdp_sla`) as the source of truth for provisioning/SLA
50	  data.
51	- Confirmed request/message flow for SMS/USSD (from `modules/sbl-v2/README.md` and
52	  `docs/flow-testing`):
53	  ```
54	  SP/App --> SDP (core) --http/https:7000--> SBL-V2 --http/https:9966--> USSD GW
55	                          <--http/https:8888--
56	                SBL-V2 --smpp:3001/3002--> SMPP server(s)
57	  ```
58	  SBL-V2 = SMS/USSD load-balancing gateway component in front of the USSD GW and SMPP servers,
59	  with its own MySQL-backed SLA data and optional one-way TLS on both the SDP↔SBL-V2 and
60	  SBL-V2↔MySQL links.
61	- `modules/mule-integration` is the core MO/MT processing engine: routes messages through SBL
62	  (queue names in `sbl.properties`), UCP/number-checking (`numberchecking.properties`), ECGS
63	  charging (`charging.properties`), and NBL (`nbl.properties`); uses RocksDB-backed queues to
64	  survive bursts/restarts without losing in-flight messages.
65	- `modules/number-checking` performs subscriber/number-type lookups against MAP GW / Sigtran GW,
66	  with a caching layer and per-NCS-type (SMS vs BAS vs USSD) fallback-to-cache configuration
67	  (see `SMS_NUMBER_CHECKING_CONFIGURATION.md`).
68	- Three modern Spring Boot apps sit behind a single Apache HTTPD reverse proxy and one Keycloak
69	  realm for SSO (confirmed in `keycloak/KEYCLOAK_SSO_GUIDE.md`):
70	  ```
71	  Browser (HTTPS :443)
72	        -> Apache HTTPD
73	             /provisioning -> https://localhost:8082/provisioning  (provisioning-v2)
74	             /report       -> https://localhost:8084/report        (report-viewer-v2)
75	             /cdrquery     -> https://localhost:8088/cdrquery      (cdrquery)
76	             /             -> https://localhost:9443/              (Keycloak)
77	  ```
78	- `HAMultiHost_Flow_Diagram.md` documents a generic high-availability multi-host client
79	  (parses a comma-separated URL list, health-checks hosts, fails over) used for outbound
80	  connector calls — check which connectors use it before assuming any single one does; not
81	  independently confirmed which callers use `HAMultiHost` beyond the diagram doc.
82	
83	## Modules / Components
84	- **provisioning-v2** — Spring Boot 3 web app (Thymeleaf) for SP/application/CR provisioning
85	  and SLA management; Keycloak OAuth2 client, HTTPS on `:8082`, context path `/provisioning`.
86	  Path: `modules/provisioning-v2`
87	- **provisioning** (legacy) — original Ant/JSP provisioning webapp, CAS-secured, being
88	  superseded by provisioning-v2. Path: `modules/provisioning`
89	- **provisioning-startup-services** — shared startup/init services consumed by
90	  provisioning(-v2). Path: `modules/provisioning-startup-services`
91	- **dashboard** — legacy Ant/JSP operational dashboard (Flash-based charts under `flash_src/`),
92	  CAS-secured. Path: `modules/dashboard`
93	- **sbl-v2** — SMS/USSD load-balancing gateway in front of USSD GW/SMPP servers; Spring-based,
94	  MySQL-backed, optional mutual TLS. Path: `modules/sbl-v2`
95	- **mule-integration** — Mule-based core MO/MT message processing engine; RocksDB-backed burst
96	  queue; integrates SBL, number-checking/UCP, ECGS charging, NBL. Path: `modules/mule-integration`
97	- **number-checking** — subscriber number-type lookup/caching against MAP GW / Sigtran GW, with
98	  per-NCS-type (SMS/BAS/USSD) config. Path: `modules/number-checking`
99	- **charging** — charging/ECGS integration logic and its own DB setup scripts. Path:
100	  `modules/charging`
101	- **core-logic** (`sdp-core-logic`) — shared domain/business logic library (Hibernate entities,
102	  services) used by provisioning, provisioning-v2, report-viewer-v2, etc. Path: `core-logic`
103	- **component-integration** — integration glue module (legacy Ant/Ivy). Path:
104	  `modules/component-integration`
105	- **cas** — CAS server assets (`cas.zip`, JSPs) for legacy-app SSO. Path: `modules/cas`
106	- **cdragent / cdragent_v2** — CDR (call/message detail record) collection agent, legacy and v2.
107	  Path: `modules/cdragent`, `modules/cdragent_v2`
108	- **reporting/report-viewer-v2** — Spring Boot 3 reporting UI (JasperReports/POI/iText exports),
109	  Keycloak OAuth2, replacing legacy `reportviewer`. Path: `modules/reporting/report-viewer-v2`
110	- **reporting/cdrquery** — Spring Boot 3 app for CDR querying, Spring Data JPA + MySQL,
111	  OAuth2 client and resource-server (JWT) support, Keycloak-secured; has its own
112	  `KEYCLOAK-REALM-SETUP.md`. Path: `modules/reporting/cdrquery`
113	- **reporting/dataloader(_v2) / datarecover(_v2) / datatransfer(_v2)** — CDR/report data ETL
114	  utilities, legacy Ant and newer Maven variants coexist. Path: `modules/reporting/*`
115	- **traffic-controller** (`traffic-notification-client`, `traffic-updater`) — traffic
116	  control/notification components, Maven-based. Path: `modules/traffic-controller`
117	- **http-ha** — HTTP high-availability library (likely backs `HAMultiHost`). Path:
118	  `modules/http-ha`
119	- **web-core** (`sdp-web-core`) — shared web layer library used by several legacy/Boot apps.
120	  Path: `modules/web-core`
121	- **hms-common-ncs-message** — shared NCS (network/content service) message model library used
122	  across protocol-api connectors. Path: `modules/hms-common-ncs-message`
123	- **protocol-api/ussd, ecgs, sigtran-gw-connector, ucp** — protocol connector libraries for

# Project Context

Last updated: 2026-09-03 (run_id 2026-09-03) — Initial creation. No prior `context.md` existed in
`/hms/projects/m1_sdp/M1-SDP/m1-sdp-qa-pipeline` at time of writing; this document was built from
scratch by reading the codebase at `/hms/projects/m1_sdp/M1-SDP/m1-sdp` (HEAD detached at tag
`3.0.68`, latest commit `2b8c7f561`).

## Overview
- **m1-sdp** (hSenid Mobile "M1 Service Delivery Platform") is a large, long-lived telecom SDP:
  it provisions and mediates value-added services (SMS, USSD, BAS/premium billing, WAP push, MMS)
  between mobile network operator gateways (SMSC/UCP, USSD GW, SS7/Sigtran, ECGS charging) and
  content/service providers, plus back-office apps for provisioning, charging config, and CDR
  reporting.
- Multi-module Maven reactor (`pom.xml`, `groupId hsenidmobile.sdp`, `artifactId m1-sdp`,
  currently version `3.0.68`) containing ~50 modules of very mixed vintage: modern Spring Boot 3
  apps sit alongside 2008-era Ant/Ivy webapps in the same repo.
- Confirmed from `README.md`: runtime is OpenJDK 21, MySQL 8.4.4, Maven 3+; legacy modules still
  build with Ant + `HSENID_BUILD_COMMON`/`CXF_HOME` env vars, and depend on external
  hSenid-internal connector projects (`ajuba-connector`, `ussd-connector`, `spml-connector`)
  built separately from their own repos.

## Tech Stack
- **Languages/runtime:** Java 21 (`pom.xml` `maven.compiler.target=21`); a few legacy modules
  historically targeted Java 1.6 (`module.properties` in `core-logic`, `compile.target.version=1.6`,
  though the parent POM now forces 21 repo-wide).
- **Modern stack (provisioning-v2, report-viewer-v2, cdrquery):** Spring Boot 3.4.5, Spring
  6.2.6, Thymeleaf + Tailwind CSS, Spring Security OAuth2 Client (Keycloak SSO), Hibernate
  6.6.13, MySQL Connector/J 9.3.0, Log4j2 2.25.1, Jasper Reports/POI/iText (report-viewer-v2),
  Spring Data JPA (cdrquery).
- **Legacy stack (dashboard, provisioning, reportviewer, cdragent, etc.):** Ant + Ivy builds,
  JSP/Struts-style webapps, CAS-based SSO (`modules/cas`), c3p0 connection pooling, ehcache.
- **Messaging/integration middleware:** Mule ESB 3.x-style custom runtime
  (`modules/mule-integration`, packaged as `sdp-mule-integration`), RocksDB used as a local
  durable queue/burst buffer (`RocksDbBasedBurstServerEventHandler.java`, plus
  `RocksDbBurstHandler_FlowDiagram.md` at repo root documenting that flow).
- **DB:** MySQL, schema name `sdp_sla` (seen in `core-logic.properties`, `sbl-v2` README),
  accessed via JDBC/Hibernate/c3p0; `docker-compose.yaml` at root spins up `mysql:5.6.51` for
  local dev alongside newer modules that assume MySQL 8.4.4 — **version mismatch, not confirmed
  which is authoritative for current dev**.
- **Build tools present:** Maven (root `pom.xml`, `mvnw`), Ant (`build.xml` at root and in most
  legacy modules), Ivy (`ivy.xml` in legacy modules), npm/Tailwind (`package.json` in
  provisioning-v2 and report-viewer-v2 for CSS build only).
- **Auth:** Keycloak OAuth2/OIDC for the three new Spring Boot apps (see Architecture), CAS for
  legacy dashboard/provisioning/reportviewer apps.

## Architecture
- Overall style: **service-oriented monolith-of-modules** — one Maven reactor, many
  independently deployable components communicating over HTTP(S), SMPP, and Mule-mediated
  queues, sharing one MySQL database (`sdp_sla`) as the source of truth for provisioning/SLA
  data.
- Confirmed request/message flow for SMS/USSD (from `modules/sbl-v2/README.md` and
  `docs/flow-testing`):
  ```
  SP/App --> SDP (core) --http/https:7000--> SBL-V2 --http/https:9966--> USSD GW
                          <--http/https:8888--
                SBL-V2 --smpp:3001/3002--> SMPP server(s)
  ```
  SBL-V2 = SMS/USSD load-balancing gateway component in front of the USSD GW and SMPP servers,
  with its own MySQL-backed SLA data and optional one-way TLS on both the SDP↔SBL-V2 and
  SBL-V2↔MySQL links.
- `modules/mule-integration` is the core MO/MT processing engine: routes messages through SBL
  (queue names in `sbl.properties`), UCP/number-checking (`numberchecking.properties`), ECGS
  charging (`charging.properties`), and NBL (`nbl.properties`); uses RocksDB-backed queues to
  survive bursts/restarts without losing in-flight messages.
- `modules/number-checking` performs subscriber/number-type lookups against MAP GW / Sigtran GW,
  with a caching layer and per-NCS-type (SMS vs BAS vs USSD) fallback-to-cache configuration
  (see `SMS_NUMBER_CHECKING_CONFIGURATION.md`).
- Three modern Spring Boot apps sit behind a single Apache HTTPD reverse proxy and one Keycloak
  realm for SSO (confirmed in `keycloak/KEYCLOAK_SSO_GUIDE.md`):
  ```
  Browser (HTTPS :443)
        -> Apache HTTPD
             /provisioning -> https://localhost:8082/provisioning  (provisioning-v2)
             /report       -> https://localhost:8084/report        (report-viewer-v2)
             /cdrquery     -> https://localhost:8088/cdrquery      (cdrquery)
             /             -> https://localhost:9443/              (Keycloak)
  ```
- `HAMultiHost_Flow_Diagram.md` documents a generic high-availability multi-host client
  (parses a comma-separated URL list, health-checks hosts, fails over) used for outbound
  connector calls — check which connectors use it before assuming any single one does; not
  independently confirmed which callers use `HAMultiHost` beyond the diagram doc.

## Modules / Components
- **provisioning-v2** — Spring Boot 3 web app (Thymeleaf) for SP/application/CR provisioning
  and SLA management; Keycloak OAuth2 client, HTTPS on `:8082`, context path `/provisioning`.
  Path: `modules/provisioning-v2`
- **provisioning** (legacy) — original Ant/JSP provisioning webapp, CAS-secured, being
  superseded by provisioning-v2. Path: `modules/provisioning`
- **provisioning-startup-services** — shared startup/init services consumed by
  provisioning(-v2). Path: `modules/provisioning-startup-services`
- **dashboard** — legacy Ant/JSP operational dashboard (Flash-based charts under `flash_src/`),
  CAS-secured. Path: `modules/dashboard`
- **sbl-v2** — SMS/USSD load-balancing gateway in front of USSD GW/SMPP servers; Spring-based,
  MySQL-backed, optional mutual TLS. Path: `modules/sbl-v2`
- **mule-integration** — Mule-based core MO/MT message processing engine; RocksDB-backed burst
  queue; integrates SBL, number-checking/UCP, ECGS charging, NBL. Path: `modules/mule-integration`
- **number-checking** — subscriber number-type lookup/caching against MAP GW / Sigtran GW, with
  per-NCS-type (SMS/BAS/USSD) config. Path: `modules/number-checking`
- **charging** — charging/ECGS integration logic and its own DB setup scripts. Path:
  `modules/charging`
- **core-logic** (`sdp-core-logic`) — shared domain/business logic library (Hibernate entities,
  services) used by provisioning, provisioning-v2, report-viewer-v2, etc. Path: `core-logic`
- **component-integration** — integration glue module (legacy Ant/Ivy). Path:
  `modules/component-integration`
- **cas** — CAS server assets (`cas.zip`, JSPs) for legacy-app SSO. Path: `modules/cas`
- **cdragent / cdragent_v2** — CDR (call/message detail record) collection agent, legacy and v2.

- **reporting/cdrquery** — Spring Boot 3 app for CDR querying, Spring Data JPA + MySQL,

- **reporting/dataloader(_v2) / datarecover(_v2) / datatransfer(_v2)** — CDR/report data ETL

  `Dockerfile.python`, own `docker-compose.yml`). Path: `mock-servers/`

  (`emailMessageTemplate.properties`, `emailGroup.properties` present) — actual SMTP
  server/config not confirmed from code alone.
- **WireMock/mock HTTP servers** — `mock-servers/` mocks an SMS delivery-report HTTP endpoint
  for local/CI testing, not a production integration.

## Test Conventions
- **Frameworks in use:** JUnit 4.12 (root `pom.xml` dependency, inherited by most Maven
  modules); JUnit 5 (Jupiter) + jmock-junit5 confirmed in `core-logic`, `modules/http-ha`,
  `modules/reporting/datarecover_v2`, `simulators/smpp-sim` — **the codebase mixes JUnit 4 and
  JUnit 5 across modules**, check per-module `pom.xml` before assuming which applies.
  `spring-boot-starter-test` (JUnit 5 + Mockito + AssertJ) is used in the three Spring Boot apps
  (provisioning-v2, report-viewer-v2, cdrquery) and `spring-security-test` in cdrquery.
- **Layout:** standard Maven `src/test/java` per module (56 modules have a `src/test` directory);
  legacy Ant modules (e.g. `qa/provisioning-automated`) use `src/test` + `src/dev` conventions
  under Ant/Ivy instead of Maven.
- **No CI pipeline file found in this repo** (`not confirmed`: no `.gitlab-ci.yml`, `Jenkinsfile`,
  or `.github/workflows` present at the time of this scan) — build/test automation, if any, is
  likely orchestrated outside this repo or not yet checked in.
- **Running tests locally:** default is `mvn clean install` per module/reactor;
  README explicitly documents `mvn clean install -Dmaven.test.skip=true` as the standard build
  command, i.e. **tests are skipped by default in the documented build flow** — a QA agent should
  not assume `mvn install` alone exercises the test suite.
- **Local environment setup for manual/integration testing** (from README + module READMEs):
  - MySQL 8.4.4 (or `docker-compose.yaml`'s MySQL 5.6.51 for a lighter local DB — version
    mismatch, confirm which the team actually uses) with `sdp_sla` schema, seeded via
    `modules/dbsetup/conf/complete-install/readme.txt` and per-module sample dumps (e.g.
    `modules/mule-integration/conf/test/sample-db-dump.sql`).
  - External connector projects must be pre-built at pinned versions: `ajuba-connector`,
    `ussd-connector`, `spml-connector` (versions pinned in root `pom.xml`).
  - Protocol simulators under `simulators/*` and mocks under `mock-servers/` stand in for real
    network elements (SMPP, USSD GW, ECGS, Sigtran GW, SMS delivery reports) during local/manual
    testing — each has its own README.
  - Keycloak + self-signed TLS certs required to exercise provisioning-v2 / report-viewer-v2 /
    cdrquery end-to-end (see `keycloak/KEYCLOAK_SSO_GUIDE.md` and per-module
    `generate-ssl-cert.sh` / `KEYCLOAK-REALM-SETUP.md`).
- **Existing manual QA assets:** `qa/Automated_Scripts/*` — a large archive of historical,
  scenario-named manual test scripts (app creation, CR flow, MO/MT-only, WAP-only, etc.) from
  prior releases; `qa/grinder` — Jython load-test scripts for SMS/MMS/WAP-push MT flows.

## Risk Notes
- **Mixed legacy/modern architecture** — Ant/Ivy/JSP/CAS modules (dashboard, provisioning,
  reportviewer, cdragent, most `protocol-api`/`ws`/`sdk` modules) coexist with new Spring Boot
  3 + Keycloak apps (provisioning-v2, report-viewer-v2, cdrquery). Migrations in progress
  ("v2" modules) mean **duplicate/parallel functionality** may exist (e.g. `provisioning` vs
  `provisioning-v2`, `reportviewer` vs `report-viewer-v2`) — confirm which is actually deployed
  before testing.
- **JDK/dependency upgrade churn** — recent commits (`git log`) show an active
  `jdk-upgrade/sdp-core` effort with jar-deduplication fixes ("Removed redundant jars with
  multiple versions: ehcache and hms-common-util", "Excluded duplicate BouncyCastle and unused
  spring-security-cas jars") — classpath/dependency-version regressions are a plausible recent
  risk area.
- **TLS/hostname-verification bugs in SBL-V2/USSD path** — recent fix commits
  (`ecf8d972f`, `6bfaaba1f`, and a revert `10e010bf9`) show SSL hostname verification and TLS
  version configuration for the ussd-connector was buggy enough that MO logs could silently show
  SUCCESS on a real SSL failure — this is a concrete, recently-touched fragile area worth
  regression testing around SBL-V2 TLS config.
- **RocksDB-backed burst queue in mule-integration** — recovery-on-restart logic
  (`RocksDbBasedBurstServerEventHandler`, documented in `RocksDbBurstHandler_FlowDiagram.md`,
  plus a 44 KB `RocksDB_Performance_Investigation.md` at repo root) indicates this area has had
  real performance/correctness investigations — treat message durability/ordering across
  restarts as a fragile area.
- **Shared single MySQL schema (`sdp_sla`)** across many modules (provisioning-v2, sbl-v2,
  mule-integration, etc.) — schema changes in one module's DB setup scripts can affect others;
  no evidence of per-module schema isolation.
- **Auth boundary duality** — CAS (legacy) vs Keycloak/OAuth2 (new apps) means session/SSO
  behavior differs by app; cdrquery is also a JWT resource server, widening its auth surface
  (token validation bugs would be distinct from the cookie-based apps).
- **Hardcoded example secrets/passwords in checked-in config** — e.g. plaintext DB password
  (`jdbc.password=password`), Keycloak client secret, and keystore passwords in
  `provisioning-v2/src/main/resources/application.yaml` and `core-logic.properties` — likely
  dev-only defaults, but flag for review; not confirmed whether production overrides these via
  externalized config.
- **External/pinned connector dependencies** (`ajuba-connector`, `ussd-connector`,
  `spml-connector`) live in separate repos and must be built at exact pinned versions — version
  drift here is a build/integration risk outside this repo's direct control.
- **No CI pipeline definition found in-repo** — regression safety net (if any) is not visible
  from the codebase itself; cannot confirm what, if anything, runs automatically on commits/PRs.

## Not Confirmed
- Whether any CI/CD pipeline (Jenkins, GitLab CI, etc.) actually runs against this repo — no
  pipeline definition file found in the working tree.
- Which MySQL version is authoritative for local dev — root `docker-compose.yaml` provisions
  `mysql:5.6.51` while README and several module READMEs (sbl-v2, mule-integration) specify
  MySQL 8.4.4.
- Whether `provisioning`/`dashboard`/`reportviewer` (legacy, CAS-based) are still actively
  deployed in production alongside their "v2" Spring Boot replacements, or fully retired.
- Actual production values for Keycloak realm/client config, SMTP server, and SNMP trap
  destinations — only dev/example values were found in checked-in `application.yaml` /
  `*.properties` files.
- Precise meaning of some project-specific acronyms (NCS, NBL, SWS, BAS) beyond what's inferable
  from config/package names — no glossary found in the repo; inferred from context (NCS ≈
  "network/content service" channel type such as SMS/BAS/USSD; BAS ≈ premium billing/bearer
  application service based on `sdk/bas`, `ws/bas` content) but not explicitly defined anywhere
  read.
- Full behavior/ownership of the `patch/`, `mule-patch/`, `native-binary/`, and `support/`
  top-level directories — appear to be historical patch sets and native library overrides but
  were not deeply inspected.

# Test Plan — m1-sdp 3.0.65 → 3.0.68 (run_id: 2026-09-03)

Based on: `output/changes.md`, `output/context.md`, `output/code-scan.md` for run `2026-09-03`.
`output/requirements.md` does not exist for this run (see CR Traceability section).
Status: DRAFT — requires human review and sign-off before test case writing begins

## Scope Summary
This release (3.0.65 → 3.0.68, 25 commits) adds SP-application-search pagination and
USSD-connector TLS hardening to sbl-v2, reworks CSV export data-fetching, adds loading
indicators and centralized error/DB-down handling to report-viewer-v2, fixes eight bugs
(SMS-MO mislogging on TLS failure, charging-SLA edit NPEs, stale USSD service-code on CR
activation, three Jasper report title/layout defects, a spurious SNMP trap on shutdown), and
carries a large wave of dependency de-duplication (ehcache, BouncyCastle, `spring-security-cas`
removal) plus a mechanical version bump across ~120 module POMs. No breaking changes were
declared, but two of the "bug fixes" change shared-method behavior (`SdpMessageSender`
rethrowing) in ways that ripple into callers not themselves changed this release, and one
enhancement (CSV export rework) silently drops previously-exported data (MMS/WAP-push) — both
are called out below as elevated-risk areas needing focused regression testing. Overall approach:
prioritize the SP-provisioning, sbl-v2 TLS/messaging, and CR-activation areas as High-risk
functional+regression testing; treat the report-viewer-v2 UI/error-handling changes as
Medium-risk regression across all report pages (broad blast radius, low data sensitivity); treat
the report-title/layout fixes and the mechanical dependency/version-bump changes as Low-risk
smoke/verification only.

## Impacted Areas

### 1. SP Application Search Pagination
- **Traces to change(s):** New Feature — "Pagination on SP application search", ref `46600a3d1`
- **Impact type:** Direct
- **Risk:** High — Code complexity: replaces the old `AppListService` entirely with a new
  paginated flow across `AppRepositoryImpl`, `SpRepositoryImpl`,
  `ApplicationListBySpUserService`, `BaseProvisioningService` (large, tangled change per
  `changes.md`). Business impact: this is a core, frequently-used provisioning screen (SP/app
  lookup). Data sensitivity: SP business data (company names, application configs), not PII/money
  directly. Module dependencies: `core-logic` repository methods are shared by other consumers
  per `context.md`'s module map — changing their query shape is a shared-dependency risk.
  **Reweighted to High by code-scan**: `code-scan.md` Should-Fix flags `page`/`size` have no
  input validation, causing invalid `LIMIT`/`OFFSET` SQL, which is swallowed by a blanket
  `catch (Throwable ex)` and rendered as a misleading "no application found" message
  (`ListAppBySpUserController.java:51-64,73-77`) — a real negative-testing/robustness gap.
- **Test scope:** Functional (page navigation, page-size selector 10/25/50/100, grouping of
  multi-app SP rows across page boundaries), negative (invalid/out-of-range `page`/`size` values,
  edited-URL tampering), regression (compare result set/row content against the old
  `AppListService` behavior for parity), integration (repository query correctness against
  `sdp_sla`).
- **Notes:** Code-scan also flags unescaped `%`/`_` wildcard characters in the SP-name search
  parameter (`AppRepositoryImpl.java:1686-1707`) — low impact but worth a quick functional check
  if SP company names can contain those characters. Whether any UI element expected an
  approval-detail affordance from the old `AppListService` that's now silently absent
  (`BaseProvisioningService.java:1265-1273`) is possible impact, needs verification.

### 2. CSV Export Bulk-Fetch Rework
- **Traces to change(s):** Enhancement — "Bulk-fetch CSV export data", ref `f0fd261ee`
- **Impact type:** Direct
- **Risk:** High — Code complexity: reworks `CsvDownLoadMangerServiceImpl`,
  `DataRetriverDao(Impl)`, `DataRetriverService(Impl)`, `ProvisioningQueries` from per-app to
  bulk queries. Business impact: CSV export is used for offline reporting/reconciliation by SP
  ops; a silent data-completeness regression here is high blast-radius. Data sensitivity: SP
  charging/application configuration data. **Reweighted to High by code-scan**: the "Business
  Rules & Behavior Discovered" section states plainly that "CSV export for SP application search
  no longer includes MMS or WAP-push data... even for apps that have those NCS types configured"
  (`CsvDownLoadMangerServiceImpl.java:47-51`) — this is an undocumented behavior change with real
  potential to break downstream consumers of the export. Additionally, a Should-Fix-adjacent Note
  flags an unbounded `IN (...)` list per export with "no chunking" acknowledged in-code as a known
  gap (`CsvDownLoadMangerServiceImpl.java:59`, `DataRetriverDaoImpl.java:~74`).
- **Test scope:** Functional (export content correctness for BAS/SMS/USSD apps), negative
  (confirm MMS/WAP-push apps export without those columns/data and this doesn't silently
  corrupt row alignment), regression (compare export output against pre-3.0.68 exports for the
  same SP/app set), performance (export against a large SP/app set to probe the unbounded
  `IN`-list limit called out in code-scan).
- **Notes:** Whether dropping MMS/WAP-push from the export is an intentional, communicated
  deprecation or an unintended regression is possible impact, needs verification — see Open
  Questions.

### 3. USSD-Connector TLS Hostname Verification & Protocol Configuration
- **Traces to change(s):** New Feature — "USSD-connector TLS hostname verification & protocol
  configuration", ref `ecf8d972f`, `10e010bf9`
- **Impact type:** Direct + Ripple
- **Risk:** High — Code complexity: moderate (config + connector version bump), but sits on a
  security-critical path. Business impact: SBL-v2 → USSD GW is a core message-delivery
  integration point per `context.md`'s architecture diagram; misconfiguration could break all
  USSD MT/MO traffic. Data sensitivity: TLS/auth boundary (transport security for subscriber
  message traffic). Module dependencies: depends on an externally-pinned `ussd-connector`
  library (1.0.86 → 1.0.89) built outside this repo — a version-drift risk `context.md` already
  flags as "Not Confirmed"/outside direct control. **Reweighted to High by defect-prone-zone
  heuristic**: `context.md`'s Risk Notes and this release's own history (`2b79211df` removed
  these properties as "dead", `10e010bf9` reverted that removal, `ecf8d972f` then built the
  feature on top) show this exact configuration was touched three times across recent releases —
  a legitimate, release-range-confirmed churn signal (not a thin/inconclusive one, since it's
  drawn directly from this release's own commit history, not aggregated external bug data).
- **Test scope:** Functional (hostname verification enabled by default, TLS protocol pinning to
  `TLSv1.3,TLSv1.2`), negative (connection to a USSD GW presenting a mismatched hostname cert
  should now fail closed, not silently succeed), integration (SBL-v2 ↔ USSD GW end-to-end using
  `simulators/hms-ussd-sim` or `ussd-gw-jetty` per `context.md`'s test conventions), regression
  (confirm this doesn't regress USSD MT/MO throughput or introduce handshake failures against a
  correctly-configured GW), security (verify the setting has no effect unless SBL-v2 is built
  against the pinned 1.0.89 connector, per code-scan's business-rule note).
- **Notes:** None outstanding — behavior is documented consistently across `changes.md` and
  `code-scan.md`.

### 4. SMS-MO Delivery-Failure Logging Fix & Shared `send()` Path
- **Traces to change(s):** Bug Fix — "SMS-MO translog falsely showed SUCCESS on SSL hostname
  verification failure", ref `6bfaaba1f`
- **Impact type:** Direct + Ripple
- **Risk:** High — Code complexity: the fix itself is small (rethrow instead of swallow in
  `SdpMessageSender`), but it changes the failure contract of a shared method with multiple
  callers. Business impact: SMS-MO transaction logging accuracy affects billing/reconciliation
  and ops visibility into real failures. Data sensitivity: message-delivery transaction records.
  Module dependencies: `SdpMessageSender.send()` is called from at least two other flows not
  themselves changed this release. **Reweighted to High by code-scan Should-Fix**: in
  `DeliverNotifyProcessor.processDeliveryReport` (`DeliverNotifyProcessor.java:300-313`), the
  now-thrown exception on a Core-unreachable delivery-report notify skips the subsequent
  `deliveryReportDao.deleteByCorrelationId(...)`, `deliverNotifyDAO.deleteByCorrelationId(...)`,
  and `checkAndUpdateBlacklist(...)` cleanup calls that used to always run — a genuine behavior
  change to an un-modified caller, exactly the kind of ripple this test plan is meant to catch.
- **Test scope:** Functional (SMS-MO translog correctly shows FAILURE with error message on TLS
  failure), regression (delivery-report cleanup/blacklist-update still runs correctly when Core
  is reachable — and explicitly, what happens to those DAO/blacklist calls when Core is
  unreachable during DR routing), integration (SmsMoMessageProcessor and DeliverNotifyProcessor
  against a simulated Core outage), negative (Core-unreachable scenarios for both MO send and DR
  notify paths).
- **Notes:** Code-scan Note also flags that `SmsMtMessageProcessor.sendFailedResp2Core` (6
  call sites) can now throw, skipping `TpsLogger.incrementSmsFailed()` — whether ops
  dashboards/alerts rely on this "failed SMS" counter is possible impact, needs verification (see
  Open Questions).

### 5. Draft SMS/USSD Charging-SLA Edit NPE Fix
- **Traces to change(s):** Bug Fix — "Fix NPEs on draft and CR charging SLA edits", ref
  `42ef3d8c1`
- **Impact type:** Direct + Ripple
- **Risk:** High — Code complexity: touches initialization-order and validation-order across
  `ApplicationRequestService`, `BaseProvisioningService`, `ListDraftAppReqController`,
  `CrDraftRejectController`, `CrRequestedAppService` (8 files). Business impact: charging SLA
  drives billing/rating for SMS and USSD services — a regression here has revenue impact. Data
  sensitivity: charging/billing configuration (money-adjacent). Module dependencies: charging SLA
  is a shared domain concept in `core-logic` used by provisioning-v2 and (per `context.md`) the
  broader charging/ECGS integration point — a change in initialization order here is exactly the
  kind of shared-data-model ripple `context.md`'s module map calls out.
- **Test scope:** Functional (draft SMS/USSD SLA edit with an MT-charging-type change no longer
  NPEs on submit), regression (CR draft-reject flow — `handleChargingSlaChange`/
  `setUpdatedNcsCharingSla` now run before validation/update; confirm no new validation-bypass or
  ordering side effects), integration (charging SLA persistence against `sdp_sla`), negative
  (submit with missing/invalid charge-type combinations).
- **Notes:** None outstanding.

### 6. CR Activation — USSD Service-Code Re-registration Fix
- **Traces to change(s):** Bug Fix — "Fix stale USSD service code registration on CR activation",
  ref `bdfbf5554`
- **Impact type:** Direct + Ripple
- **Risk:** High — Code complexity: touches identity-swap logic across
  `BaseProvisioningService`, `CrApprovedAppReqService`, `CrApprovedProductionService`,
  `CrPreActiveProductionService` (new unit tests added, a positive coverage signal). Business
  impact: CR activation to testbed/production is a live, largely irreversible operation on real
  SP service codes — getting the old/new service-code swap wrong directly caused the bug being
  fixed. Data sensitivity: production service-code registration state. Module dependencies: the
  state-change event is now published only after DB commit (timing change) — per `context.md`'s
  architecture, `mule-integration`/downstream consumers of provisioning state-change events are
  a plausible audience, though `context.md` does not explicitly confirm subscribers of this
  specific event.
- **Test scope:** Functional (CR activation correctly unregisters the pre-swap/old USSD service
  code, not the already-swapped one), regression (production `additionalInfo` map is no longer
  overwritten by form binding), integration (state-change event timing relative to commit — no
  event should fire on a rolled-back transaction), negative (activation failure/rollback
  scenarios).
- **Notes:** Whether any downstream consumer depends on the state-change event's previous
  (pre-commit) timing is possible impact, needs verification — see Open Questions.

### 7. Report Pages — Loading Indicator
- **Traces to change(s):** Enhancement — "Loading indicators on report view/download", ref
  `10e722904`, `a0f4927ca`
- **Impact type:** Direct
- **Risk:** Medium — Code complexity: a shared fragment wired into every daily/weekly/monthly/
  yearly report page (broad surface, but each integration is repetitive/similar). Business
  impact: UX-only, no data correctness at stake. Data sensitivity: none. Module dependencies:
  touches all report-viewer-v2 view pages, so a regression here is broad but shallow.
  **Reweighted upward within Medium by defect-prone-zone signal**: this feature already needed a
  same-release follow-up fix (`a0f4927ca`, "across 12+ daily/hourly/monthly report pages") — a
  release-range-confirmed churn signal indicating the initial implementation had real
  page-by-page inconsistencies.
- **Test scope:** Functional (spinner shows after the documented 300ms threshold, not before;
  buttons/dropdowns disable while loading), regression (auto re-enable after 60s on a hung
  request — verify actual behavior when a request never returns), regression across all
  daily/weekly/monthly/yearly report page types (not just one representative page, given the
  follow-up-fix history).
- **Notes:** None outstanding.

### 8. Report Pages — Centralized Exception Handling
- **Traces to change(s):** Enhancement — "Global exception handling for report-viewer-v2", ref
  `ce807dfda`
- **Impact type:** Direct + Ripple
- **Risk:** Medium — Code complexity: new `GlobalExceptionHandler`/`ReportErrorMessages`,
  extended `CustomErrorController`. Business impact: every report view/download/generate request
  and the three in-page XHR endpoints (`/loadApplications`, `/loadServiceTypes`,
  `/testSummaryDataStatus`) now route through this shared handler — broad blast radius across
  all of report-viewer-v2. Data sensitivity: none directly, but a mis-routed error response could
  mask a real data problem. Module dependencies: overlaps with Area 9 below (both touch
  report-controller error paths) — the two need to be tested together for interaction, not just
  individually.
- **Test scope:** Functional (unhandled exception renders the generic "Report service is
  temporarily unavailable" HTTP 500 page for full-page requests), integration (the 3 XHR
  endpoints return the parseable `<sdp-error>` XML body, not the HTML error page, so existing JS
  response-parsing doesn't break), regression (confirm normal/successful report generation is
  unaffected by the new handler), negative (simulate DB-down and other exception types across
  representative report controllers).
- **Notes:** None outstanding.

### 9. Report Pages — DB-Down Error Handling Refactor
- **Traces to change(s):** Enhancement — "Refactored DB-down error handling across report
  controllers", ref `917aa5c3e`
- **Impact type:** Direct + Ripple
- **Risk:** Medium — Code complexity: consolidates duplicated logic out of ~19 individual
  report controllers into `DatabaseConfig` — a wide-reaching refactor by file count. Business
  impact: DB-down is the exact scenario Area 10 (SNMP trap) and Area 8 (global exception handler)
  also touch — three separate changes converge on the same failure scenario this release, raising
  the importance of an integrated DB-down regression pass. Data sensitivity: none directly.
  Module dependencies: `reporting/datatransfer_v2` is also named in `changes.md` as affected,
  alongside report-viewer-v2.
- **Test scope:** Regression (DB-down behavior across all ~19 refactored controllers —
  daily/hourly/monthly/weekly/yearly — must remain consistent with pre-refactor behavior, just
  centralized), integration (interaction with Area 8's `GlobalExceptionHandler` and Area 10's
  SNMP suppression on the same DB-down code path), functional (error message content/format
  parity with the old per-controller implementations).
- **Notes:** Possible impact, needs verification: whether `reporting/datatransfer_v2`'s own
  consumers (outside report-viewer-v2) are affected by the `DatabaseConfig` changes — `changes.md`
  names it as affected but gives no detail on datatransfer_v2-specific behavior.

### 10. Report Pages — SNMP DB-Down Trap Suppression on Shutdown
- **Traces to change(s):** Bug Fix — "SNMP trap on DB-connection shutdown removed", ref
  `cc8ce3cef`
- **Impact type:** Direct
- **Risk:** Medium — Code complexity: adds `ApplicationShutdownState` to distinguish
  shutdown-triggered disconnects from real failures, plus new unit tests
  (`ConnectionListenerShutdownTest`, `GlobalExceptionHandlerTest`) — a positive coverage signal.
  Business impact: this is an ops-monitoring correctness change, not user-facing, but an
  over-broad suppression could hide a real production DB outage from NMS/ops alerting — a
  meaningful operational risk despite no direct user or revenue impact. Data sensitivity: none.
  Module dependencies: shares the DB-down code path with Areas 8 and 9.
- **Test scope:** Functional (trap correctly suppressed for a normal application shutdown),
  regression (trap still fires for a genuine DB outage while the app is running — this is the
  higher-risk direction to verify, since a false negative here hides real incidents), integration
  (with the added `ConnectionListenerShutdownTest` coverage as a baseline, not a substitute for
  manual verification against a real SNMP trap receiver).
- **Notes:** None outstanding.

### 11. Jasper Report Title/Column-Header Fixes
- **Traces to change(s):** Bug Fix — "Report title/column-header fixes", ref `cb6cd966b`,
  `cf3211d07`, `ec1b04097`
- **Impact type:** Direct
- **Risk:** Low — Code complexity: narrow, cosmetic `.jrxml` label/layout edits. Business
  impact: limited to display correctness on specific report titles/headers (Application Revenue
  Summary, Revenue TopUp Summary, Application Traffic Summary Month, Detailed Application
  Traffic Report Month/Year). Data sensitivity: none — display-only, no underlying data
  changed. Module dependencies: none beyond the individual report definitions.
- **Test scope:** Functional (correct title text renders on each named report; column headers no
  longer cut off), regression (spot-check that data values on these specific reports are
  unaffected, since only titles/headers changed).
- **Notes:** `changes.md` notes `cb6cd966b` and `cf3211d07` had terse commit messages and were
  categorized by reading the `.jrxml` diffs directly — low residual risk but flagging the
  thinner-than-usual paper trail.

### 12. Application Traffic Summary HTML Layout Overflow Fix
- **Traces to change(s):** Bug Fix — "Application traffic summary HTML layout overflow", ref
  `28e471aed`
- **Impact type:** Direct
- **Risk:** Low — Code complexity: coordinate/CSS-wrapping fix in one Jasper report service.
  Business impact: display-only (long application names no longer overflow their cells). Data
  sensitivity: none. Module dependencies: none.
- **Test scope:** Functional (long Application ID/Name values wrap correctly in the HTML-rendered
  version of this specific report), regression (PDF/other export formats of the same report still
  render correctly, since the fix was noted as "HTML-only wrapping styles").
- **Notes:** None outstanding.

### 13. Dependency De-duplication & `spring-security-cas` Removal (16+ modules)
- **Traces to change(s):** Config/Infra — "Deduplicated ehcache/hms-common-util jars",
  "Deduplicated jars in report-viewer-v2", "Excluded duplicate BouncyCastle jars and unused
  spring-security-cas", refs `c57f0b16`, `41bab91ab`, `e18e3a8b7`
- **Impact type:** Direct + Ripple
- **Risk:** Medium overall, with the `spring-security-cas` removal sub-item at Medium-High —
  Code complexity: mechanical dependency-exclusion changes across `core-logic`, `charging`,
  `component-integration`, `hms-common-ncs-message`, `http-ha`, `mule-integration`,
  `number-checking`, `performance`, `provisioning-startup-services`, `provisioning-v2`,
  `reporting/cdrquery`, `reporting/dataloader_v2`, `reporting/datarecover_v2`,
  `reporting/datatransfer_v2`, `sbl-v2`, `snmp`, `traffic-notification-client`,
  `traffic-controller/traffic-updater`. Business impact: jar-resolution changes risk
  `ClassNotFoundException`/`NoSuchMethodError` at runtime if an excluded transitive dependency
  was actually needed by code not exercised in a quick smoke test — `context.md`'s own Risk Notes
  section already flags "JDK/dependency upgrade churn... classpath/dependency-version
  regressions are a plausible recent risk area." Data sensitivity/auth: `e18e3a8b7` removes
  `spring-security-cas` from `sdp-web-core` on the stated basis that "CAS auth is no longer used
  in report-viewer-v2" — but `context.md`'s module map describes `web-core`/`sdp-web-core` as "a
  shared web layer library used by several legacy/Boot apps," and separately lists
  `dashboard`/`provisioning`(legacy)/`reportviewer` as still CAS-secured. Module dependencies:
  this is the clearest case in this release of a shared-library change with a real cross-module
  auth-boundary question attached.
- **Test scope:** Functional smoke test (application startup/context-load for every one of the
  16+ listed modules, to catch missing-transitive-dependency failures), integration
  (report-viewer-v2's own OAuth2/Keycloak login still works post-removal, since that's its
  documented auth mechanism), regression (confirm CAS-based login for the legacy `dashboard`/
  `provisioning`/`reportviewer` apps is unaffected if — and only if confirmed — they depend on the
  same `sdp-web-core` artifact whose CAS dependency was pruned).
- **Notes:** Possible impact, needs verification: whether legacy CAS-secured apps share the same
  `sdp-web-core` build artifact that had `spring-security-cas` removed, or use an independent
  dependency set — see Open Questions.

### 14. Reactor-Wide Version Bump (~120 module POMs)
- **Traces to change(s):** Config/Infra — "Full module version bump across the reactor to
  3.0.68", ref full range diff `3.0.65..3.0.68`
- **Impact type:** Direct
- **Risk:** Low — Code complexity: `changes.md` itself describes this as "largely version-string
  churn, not independently reviewed line-by-line beyond the itemized commits above." Business
  impact: none expected if purely version strings. Data sensitivity: none. Module dependencies:
  reactor-wide, but mechanical.
- **Test scope:** Build/packaging smoke test only (full `mvn clean install` reactor build
  succeeds at 3.0.68 across all modules) — no functional test scope beyond confirming the build
  is coherent.
- **Notes:** Per `context.md`'s Test Conventions, the documented build command
  (`mvn clean install -Dmaven.test.skip=true`) skips tests by default — the build-success smoke
  check alone does not exercise unit tests; note this in the exit-criteria discussion with the

## Out of Scope

line-by-line (mechanical, matches `changes.md`'s own caveat).

`changes.md` entry, and every file/module `changes.md` names is confirmed present in the diff.

Analyzed: 2026-09-04
Status: ADVISORY — feeds test-planner's risk rating; does not block the pipeline

## Should-Fix

- **`modules/sbl-v2/src/main/java/com/hms/sbl/v2/services/processor/impl/smpp/SdpMessageSender.java:42`**
  — The MO-log fix now rethrows on send failure (`throw new RuntimeException(e)`). This is correct
  for the intended target (`SmsMoMessageProcessor`, which now correctly logs the transaction as
  FAILED), but the same `send()` method is also used to notify Core of an inbound delivery report
  (DR). In `DeliverNotifyProcessor.processDeliveryReport` (not itself changed by this release, but
  a live caller of the changed method) the call to `deliverSmNotifyRouter.route(...)` sits ahead of
  the delivery-report/`DeliverNotify` row cleanup and blacklist-update calls, all inside one
  try/catch — see `modules/sbl-v2/src/main/java/com/hms/sbl/v2/services/processor/impl/smpp/DeliverNotifyProcessor.java:300-313`.
  Before this release, a failed "notify Core" call was swallowed and cleanup always ran; now, if
  Core is unreachable when a delivery report is being routed, the exception skips
  `deliveryReportDao.deleteByCorrelationId(...)`, `deliverNotifyDAO.deleteByCorrelationId(...)`
  and `checkAndUpdateBlacklist(...)` for that delivery report. Testers should verify whether this
  is intended (retry-preserving) behavior or an unintended side effect — if unintended, delivery
  report rows could accumulate / be reprocessed after a transient Core outage in a way they didn't
  before. Related change: `6bfaaba1f`
- **`modules/provisioning-v2/src/main/java/hsenidmobile/sdp/provisioning/v2/controller/sp/ListAppBySpUserController.java:51-64`**
  — The new `page`/`size` request parameters (used to build `LIMIT :size OFFSET :offset` in
  `AppRepositoryImpl.findProvisionedAppDTOsBySpNameSearch`, `core-logic/.../AppRepositoryImpl.java:1692-1704`)
  have no validation: a user who edits the URL to pass `page=-1` or `size=0`/a negative size gets
  an invalid SQL `LIMIT`/`OFFSET`, which throws inside `ApplicationListBySpUserService.findApplication`.
  That exception is caught by the controller's blanket `catch (Throwable ex)`
  (`ListAppBySpUserController.java:73-77`) and silently rendered as the generic "no application
  found" message — the same message shown for a genuinely empty search. A tester crafting such a
  URL (or a broken pagination link) sees a misleading "no results" instead of an error, and this
  masks the real problem in the logs only. Related change: `46600a3d1`

## Business Rules & Behavior Discovered

- **Paginated SP-application search** — `/listAppBySpUser` now accepts `page` (0-based, default
  `0`) and `size` (default `10`) query params; the UI offers a page-size selector of 10/25/50/100
  per page. `size` means rows of matching *applications* per page (not SPs matched) — a page always

  (`modules/provisioning-v2/.../controller/sp/ListAppBySpUserController.java:48-58`,

  `modules/provisioning-v2/.../templates/serviceProvider/listApplicationBySpUser.html:77-90`)
- **CSV export for SP application search no longer includes MMS or WAP-push data** — the bulk
  rewrite of `downloadApplicationForSp` only fetches/populates BAS, SMS and USSD charging details;
  MMS and WAP-push are explicitly called out as deprecated and no longer populated in the exported
  CSV, even for apps that have those NCS types configured.

  `ussd-connector.ssl.enabled-protocols`. This is enforced by the external `ussd-connector` library

  against that pinned connector version.
  (`modules/sbl-v2/src/main/java/com/hms/sbl/v2/configuration/Configuration.java:81,93,282-283`,
  `modules/sbl-v2/src/main/resources/application.yaml:127-133`)

  SSL hostname-verification failure), the transaction log now correctly records `FAILURE` with the
  underlying error message instead of `SUCCESS`.
  (`modules/sbl-v2/.../smpp/SdpMessageSender.java:42`,
  `modules/sbl-v2/.../smpp/SmsMoMessageProcessor.java:79-84`)
- **Report pages: busy indicator** — "View"/"Download" buttons (and the dependent dropdowns) on
  every daily/weekly/monthly/yearly report page now disable themselves and show a spinner, but only
  if the request takes longer than 300ms (so a fast response never flickers). If a request hangs,
  controls are automatically re-enabled after 60 seconds regardless of whether a response ever
  arrives. (`modules/reporting/report-viewer-v2/.../templates/fragments/loading.html:60-121`)
- **Report pages: centralized error handling** — any unhandled exception from a report
  view/download/generate request (typically a DB-down condition) now renders a generic "Report
  service is temporarily unavailable. Please try again later." page (HTTP 500) instead of a blank
  tab. The three in-page XHR endpoints (`/loadApplications`, `/loadServiceTypes`,
  `/testSummaryDataStatus`) instead get a parseable XML error body
  (`<sdp-error><status>error</status></sdp-error>`) so their JS response-parsing doesn't break.
  (`modules/reporting/report-viewer-v2/.../controller/GlobalExceptionHandler.java:38-64`,
  `.../controller/CustomErrorController.java:20-63`)
- **SNMP DB-down trap suppressed during normal shutdown** — the "DB connection down" SNMP trap
  (and its log line) is now suppressed for connection teardown that happens as part of a normal
  application shutdown; it still fires for a real DB outage while the app is running.
  (`modules/reporting/report-viewer-v2/.../config/ApplicationShutdownState.java`,
  `.../config/ConnectionListener.java:60-65`, `.../config/DbConnectionHealthScheduler.java:56-59`)
- **CR activation: USSD service-code re-registration fixed** — when a CR (change request) is
  activated to testbed or production, the app's identity swap now captures the *old* USSD service
  code before the swap and passes it through, so the correct old registration is unregistered
  (previously the already-swapped/new code was passed, effectively a no-op that left the real old
  registration behind). The resulting state-change event is now published only after the DB
  transaction commits, not before.
  (`modules/provisioning-v2/.../service/BaseProvisioningService.java:2893-2930`,
  `.../service/CrApprovedAppReqService.java:391-442`,
  `.../service/CrApprovedProductionService.java:93-124`)
- **Draft SMS/USSD MT-charging-SLA edit NPE fix** — when editing a draft application's SMS or USSD
  SLA and changing the MT charging type from what was previously on the draft, the charging SLA is
  now (re-)initialized before validation runs, preventing an NPE that previously occurred on
  submit. (`modules/provisioning-v2/.../controller/application/ListDraftAppReqController.java:276-280,375-380`)

- **Pagination on SP application search** — Added pagination to the service-provider application
  search/listing flow; backing repository methods (`AppRepositoryImpl`,
  `SpRepositoryImpl`) and the `ApplicationListBySpUserService`/`BaseProvisioningService` were
  restructured to support it, replacing the old `AppListService`. Affected: `provisioning-v2`

  support (`ussd-connector.ssl.hostname-verification-enabled`,

  verification and pin allowed TLS versions (defaults to `TLSv1.3,TLSv1.2`); bumped

# Test Cases — SP Application Search Pagination

Run ID: 2026-09-03
Scope Area: SP Application Search Pagination (Test Plan Area 1)
Traces to change(s): `46600a3d1`
Risk: High

> Note: `templates/test-case.template.md` was not found in the repository for this run; the
> structure below follows the format implied by the pipeline's process instructions
> (Preconditions / numbered Steps / Expected Result per step, classification fields per case).

---

## TC-01-01 — Default pagination shows exactly one page of results

- **Priority:** High
- **Origin:** Implementation-based
- **Traces To:** `ApplicationListBySpUserService.java:76-92`
- **Category:** Functional
- **Automation Candidate:** Yes — stable, deterministic UI flow, good regression candidate.
- **Preconditions:** Logged into provisioning-v2 (`:8082`) as an authorized provisioning user; at
  least 25 applications exist across multiple SPs matching a known search term.
- **Steps:**
  1. Navigate to the SP Application Search page and search using a term that matches more than 10
     applications.
     **Expected:** Results page loads showing exactly 10 application rows (the default page
     size), with a pagination control visible.
  2. Click "Next" / page 2.
     **Expected:** Page 2 loads showing the next set of application rows (up to 10), with none
     repeated from page 1.

## TC-01-02 — Page-size selector changes the number of rows displayed

- **Priority:** High
- **Origin:** Implementation-based
- **Traces To:** `listApplicationBySpUser.html:77-90`
- **Category:** Functional
- **Automation Candidate:** Yes — deterministic row-count assertion per selector value.
- **Preconditions:** Same search term as TC-01-01, with at least 60 matching applications.
- **Steps:**
  1. Search for the term, then set the page-size selector to 25.
     **Expected:** Page reloads showing exactly 25 application rows.
  2. Set the page-size selector to 50.
     **Expected:** Page reloads showing exactly 50 application rows.
  3. Set the page-size selector to 100.
     **Expected:** Page reloads showing exactly 100 application rows (or all remaining matches if
     fewer than 100 exist).

## TC-01-03 — Applications for the same SP remain grouped across a page boundary

- **Priority:** High
- **Origin:** Implementation-based
- **Traces To:** `ApplicationListBySpUserService.java:76-92` (size counts application rows, not
  SPs; consecutive rows for the same SP are grouped for display after fetch)
- **Category:** Boundary
- **Automation Candidate:** No — requires curated seed data engineered so one SP's apps straddle
  a page boundary, plus visual/grouping judgment.
- **Preconditions:** A single SP ("Acme Corp") has more applications than fit at the end of a
  page at the default page size (e.g., seeded so its apps land at positions 9-12 of the result
  set).
- **Steps:**
  1. Search so "Acme Corp"'s applications span the page 1/page 2 boundary, then view page 1.
     **Expected:** All "Acme Corp" applications shown on page 1 are grouped together, not
     interleaved with other SPs' rows.
  2. View page 2.
     **Expected:** Any remaining "Acme Corp" applications appear grouped together at the start of
     page 2, and no application row is duplicated between page 1 and page 2.

## TC-01-04 — Negative: invalid (negative) page number via tampered URL

- **Priority:** High
- **Origin:** Implementation-based
- **Traces To:** `ListAppBySpUserController.java:51-64,73-77` (code-scan Should-Fix)
- **Category:** Negative
- **Automation Candidate:** Yes — deterministic malformed-input regression check once expected
  behavior is confirmed.
- **Preconditions:** Logged in as above; at least one matching application exists for a known,
  non-empty search term.
- **Steps:**
  1. Perform the normal search from TC-01-01 (which returns results), then edit the page URL to
     set the page number to `-1` and load it.
     **Expected:** [ASSUMPTION: pending Product/Dev answer to test-plan Open Question #2] A
     distinct error/warning message is expected, separate from "no application found." If the
     current build instead shows the generic "no application found" message for this
     known-non-empty search, record this as the current (unresolved) behavior against Open
     Question #2 rather than a hard pass/fail.

## TC-01-05 — Negative: zero/negative page size via tampered URL

- **Priority:** High
- **Origin:** Implementation-based
- **Traces To:** `ListAppBySpUserController.java:51-64,73-77`
- **Category:** Negative
- **Automation Candidate:** Yes
- **Preconditions:** Same as TC-01-04.
- **Steps:**
  1. Edit the page URL to set page size to `0` and load it.
     **Expected:** Same handling expected as TC-01-04 — a distinct error/warning, pending Open
     Question #2; record actual behavior if it instead shows "no application found."
  2. Edit the page URL to set page size to a negative value and load it.
     **Expected:** No unhandled server error page is shown, and behavior is consistent with step
     1.

## TC-01-06 — Edge: SP name search containing SQL wildcard characters

- **Priority:** Medium
- **Origin:** Implementation-based
- **Traces To:** `AppRepositoryImpl.java:1686-1707` (code-scan Note)
- **Category:** Boundary
- **Automation Candidate:** Yes — deterministic input-character check once expected match

- **Preconditions:** At least one SP whose name contains a literal `%` or `_` character, plus

     than literals per code-scan's finding.

## TC-01-07 — Regression: paginated results match legacy (pre-3.0.68) result set

- **Priority:** High
- **Origin:** Implementation-based
- **Traces To:** SP Application Search Pagination (test-plan regression scope)
- **Category:** Regression
- **Automation Candidate:** No — requires manual comparison against a legacy reference dataset;

     ordering/grouping differences are acceptable, but no application is missing or duplicated.

## TC-01-08 — Boundary: last page shows only the remaining partial rows

- **Origin:** Implementation-based

     **Expected:** The last page shows only the remaining applications (e.g., 3 rows), and no
     "Next" page control is offered.

## TC-01-09 — Functional: results-row content parity for the removed approval-detail affordance

- **Priority:** Medium
- **Origin:** Implementation-based

- **Steps:**

Traces to change(s): `ecf8d972f`, `10e010bf9`
Risk: High

## TC-03-01 — Positive: hostname verification passes for a matching certificate

- **Priority:** High
- **Origin:** Implementation-based
- **Traces To:** `Configuration.java:81,93,282-283`, `application.yaml:127-133`
- **Category:** Security
- **Automation Candidate:** Yes — deterministic TLS handshake pass/fail check, good regression
  candidate.
- **Preconditions:** SBL-v2 built against `ussd-connector` 1.0.89; a USSD GW simulator (e.g.,
  `hms-ussd-sim`) configured with a TLS certificate whose hostname matches SBL-v2's configured GW
  address; hostname-verification setting left at its default (enabled).
- **Steps:**
  1. Send a USSD MT message through SBL-v2 to the USSD GW simulator.
     **Expected:** The TLS handshake succeeds and the message is delivered successfully, with no
     hostname-verification failure logged.

## TC-03-02 — Negative/Security: connection fails closed for a mismatched-hostname certificate

- **Priority:** High
- **Origin:** Implementation-based
- **Traces To:** `Configuration.java:81,93,282-283`; `context.md` Risk Notes (TLS
  hostname-verification bugs)
- **Category:** Security
- **Automation Candidate:** Yes — this is the core regression target for the previously-fixed
  silent-success bug; deterministic and high-value to automate.
- **Preconditions:** Same as TC-03-01, but the USSD GW simulator presents a TLS certificate for a
  hostname that does NOT match SBL-v2's configured GW address.
- **Steps:**
  1. Send a USSD MT message through SBL-v2 to the mismatched-hostname simulator.
     **Expected:** The TLS handshake fails and the message send fails — it must NOT be reported
     as a successful delivery.
  2. Check the SBL-v2 MO/MT transaction log for this attempt.
     **Expected:** The log correctly records a FAILURE (with a hostname-verification/TLS error
     message), not SUCCESS.

## TC-03-03 — Functional: default TLS protocol list is restricted to TLSv1.3/TLSv1.2

- **Priority:** High
- **Origin:** Implementation-based
- **Traces To:** `application.yaml:127-133`
- **Category:** Functional
- **Automation Candidate:** Yes
- **Preconditions:** `ussd-connector.ssl.enabled-protocols` left unset (default); USSD GW
  simulator capable of reporting the negotiated protocol version.
- **Steps:**
  1. Send a USSD MT message through SBL-v2 with default configuration.
     **Expected:** The connection negotiates using TLSv1.3 or TLSv1.2 only; no other protocol
     version is reported as offered/accepted.

## TC-03-04 — Negative/Security: connection using a disallowed TLS protocol is rejected

- **Priority:** High
- **Origin:** Implementation-based
- **Traces To:** `application.yaml:127-133`
- **Category:** Security
- **Automation Candidate:** Yes
- **Preconditions:** USSD GW simulator configured to only offer an older protocol (e.g.,
  TLSv1.1) not in the default allowed list.
- **Steps:**
  1. Attempt to send a USSD MT message through SBL-v2 to this simulator.
     **Expected:** The TLS handshake fails; no message is delivered, and the failure is logged.

## TC-03-05 — Regression: USSD MT/MO throughput/handshake success unaffected against a correctly configured GW

- **Priority:** High
- **Origin:** Implementation-based
- **Traces To:** USSD-Connector TLS Hostname Verification & Protocol Configuration (test-plan
  regression scope)
- **Category:** Regression
- **Automation Candidate:** No — throughput comparison requires judgment on acceptable variance
  and a load-testing setup.
- **Preconditions:** USSD GW simulator/environment correctly configured with a valid, matching
  certificate; a baseline throughput/handshake-failure figure from the pre-3.0.68 build, if
  available.
- **Steps:**
  1. Send a representative volume of USSD MT and MO messages through SBL-v2 to the correctly
     configured GW over a fixed time window.
     **Expected:** All messages complete their TLS handshake successfully, and overall
     throughput/handshake-failure rate is comparable to the pre-3.0.68 baseline.

## TC-03-06 — Security: hostname-verification setting has no effect without the pinned connector version

- **Priority:** Medium
- **Origin:** Implementation-based
- **Traces To:** `Configuration.java:81,93,282-283` (code-scan business-rule note)
- **Category:** Security
- **Automation Candidate:** No — requires building/deploying a variant pinned to the older
  connector version; an infrequent one-off build-verification check.
- **Preconditions:** A build of SBL-v2 pinned to the older `ussd-connector` version (1.0.86) with
  hostname verification explicitly enabled in configuration.
- **Steps:**
  1. Repeat the mismatched-hostname scenario from TC-03-02 against this older-connector build.
     **Expected:** [ASSUMPTION: exact fallback behavior with the old connector is not detailed in
     the test plan] Document whether the connection still silently succeeds despite the enabled
     config setting, confirming code-scan's note that the setting is inert without the 1.0.89
     connector — record as a deployment-verification finding rather than a functional defect.

## TC-03-07 — Integration: end-to-end SBL-v2 to USSD GW MT/MO message flow

- **Priority:** High
- **Origin:** Implementation-based
- **Traces To:** USSD-Connector TLS Hostname Verification & Protocol Configuration (test-plan
  integration scope)
- **Category:** Functional
- **Automation Candidate:** Yes
- **Preconditions:** SBL-v2, USSD GW simulator (`hms-ussd-sim` or `ussd-gw-jetty`), and a
  subscriber MSISDN configured end-to-end.
- **Steps:**
  1. Initiate a USSD MO session from the simulator through SBL-v2.
     **Expected:** The MO request reaches SBL-v2 and is routed onward correctly under the new TLS
     configuration.
  2. Send a corresponding USSD MT response back through SBL-v2 to the simulator.
     **Expected:** The MT message is delivered to the simulator successfully over the newly
     configured TLS connection.

  monitoring.

     is written, for this shutdown-triggered disconnect.

  SNMP receiver.

     shutdown-triggered disconnect (no spurious trap fires), and no unhandled error/race
     condition occurs during shutdown.
